claim: For the open N-site XX chain H_N(lambda)=-J sum_i(XX+YY)+4JM-lambda M/(N+1)^2+W_N at beta=tau(N+1)^2, fixed J,tau>0 and fixed B<infinity, every lambda-independent diagonal W_N with W_N-W_N(0)I>=0 obeys the explicit uniform low-occupation tail bound F(q,A,d) and D-label trace-norm bounds in RESULT.txt, for all N, |lambda|<=B and 1<=d<=N.
supplied_inputs: public lambda-independent W_N diagonal in n_i
vacuum is a global minimizer of W_N
proof: Exact M-sector decomposition; open-chain Jordan-Wigner plus sine-mode XX spectrum; sectorwise Weyl/Courant-Fischer eigenvalue comparison Z^W_m<=Z^XX_m; vacuum denominator lower bound 1; generating-function Chernoff with s=2 tau J d^2 and explicit split at floor(d/2); overflow mixture identity ||rho-rho_tilde||_1=P_tail||rho_tail-sigma||_1<=2P_tail.

costs.memory: ceil(log2 D) archive bits; ideal total-M QND measurement uses O(N log N) elementary reversible gates and O(log N) scratch bits under a standard population counter
costs.decoder: No efficient preparation or finite-bit precision bound for omega_m is proved; generic dense diagonalization of a sector costs O(binomial(N,m)^3) arithmetic before synthesis
costs.proof: O(d) terms for explicit tail evaluation; bound is independent of range, inhomogeneity and strength of W_N

falsifier_or_failure_scope: Fails if vacuum-minimum condition is removed, if W_N depends on unknown lambda, if J_N or tau_N lose fixed positive lower bounds, or if B_N grows. Does not claim global efficient Gibbs preparation or archive optimality.

claim: The same uniform low-M tail transfer does not follow from W_N>=0 as an operator alone.
counterexample: W_N=N^2 sum_i(1-n_i)=N^2(N-M), lambda=0. It is nonnegative and range zero, but its minimum is at M=N. For M=N-k, every energy is at least E_N+(N^2-4J)k-2J(N-1), E_N=4JN. Hence Delta_N=N^2-2JN-2J separates every M<N state from the full sector for large N, and P(M<N)<=(2^N-1)exp[-tau(N+1)^2 Delta_N]->0.
falsifier_or_failure_scope: Refutes the low-occupation overflow proof under operator nonnegativity alone; it does not rule out a code centered on the known high-occupation sector.
finite_check: At N=4,J=tau=1,beta=25,U_N=16 the script finds P(M<4)=7.03e-96 and P(M>=1)=1 to double precision.
